pages.name: The second step, every state, the phone

artboards.title: As it stands today — eight faults, and the first four are the same fault
Proposed — a naming form, sized to the thing it names
Step 2 — twenty-four variants as a table, not as twenty-four cards
Empty · refused · a name too long · sizes chosen and settings set
The phone — its own design, not the desktop reflowed

annotations.text:
The brief, as answered:
· Adding is a naming errand — pricing and photos come later, and rarely at add time.
· Photo, Markup and Agent share are almost never set here → one collapsed door.
· Variable products reach 20–40 variants → a dense table, on its own step.
· The owner does this at the desk → the desktop console leads.

What the proposal costs:
· The modal widens between the steps (720 → 1160). A simple product never sees it.
· Sub-category, description and notes are still on the first screen — they were not moved behind the door, because they are how a product is found again.
· Nothing here adds a colour, a font size, or a fourteenth button family.

Secondary, by the owner's own account. It is here to prove the desktop decisions survive a switch rather than a reflow: 48px controls, the choice as full-width rows, Save in the thumb zone, and Sub-category folded away because a phone screen has no room for a field that only helps search.

The table is the single biggest win in this review: 24 stacked cards is roughly 9,800px of scrolling inside a modal, and no way to see which two of the twenty-four were given their own markup. The table answers that without moving.
